## ESCALATE — the work is sound; one hunk in it is the maintainer's call

Reviewer of record: devx lane PM, session `session_01PfaSTikked61BkcsB5Rn69`, round 13. **This is not a REWORK** — nothing is wrong with the delivery. One line in it lands on the maintainer's manual floor, so I have no authority to bless it.

### The engineering: ACCEPT on the merits

| criterion | reading |
|---|---|
| PR shape | #12768 · draft ✓ · base `main` ✓ · first line `Fixes #12555` ✓ |
| scope | 3 files, +198/−7 — the two declared gates plus **one comment-only** change in `datasource-admin-plugin.test.ts` (verified: `git diff` of that file contains no non-comment line) |
| changeset | `skip-changeset` correct |
| lint | ⭐ `pnpm lint` run **whole-repo** (`VERDICT command-exit 0`, 1m42s) — **no narrowing claimed**, unlike the other two PRs this round |

**Both halves of my dispatch measurement were re-derived and confirmed, with a correction I got wrong:** I said the two files carry the "byte-identical" alternative. Precisely, the *defective first alternative* is byte-identical (md5 `03ed0813…` both sides) but the **full** regexes are not — `check-type-source-resolution`'s dynamic-import alternative admits `:` and `<` as leading delimiters so `import('y').X` is seen in a type annotation and inside a generic argument. Only the shared first alternative was changed, and those extra delimiters are now **pinned** so a future "sync the two gates" edit cannot quietly drop them. That is a better outcome than the shared fix I assumed.

⭐ **My Zone-2 mechanism assumption was killed in the safe direction, by measurement.** I flagged that I had *not* checked whether `check-type-source-resolution` has a consumer depending on the over-greedy behaviour, and said to split if so. The dev checked: `extractTypeImports` reads only the specifier captures and never `match[1]`, so the shared fix can only ever **add** a specifier there, never remove one. Split correctly declined.

⭐ **And it rejected the shape the card floated, on measurement.** The card suggested a `;`-excluding class. Measured partial: under ASI there is no terminator for a `;`-class to stop on and the unbounded span returns. `[^;'"]` — the class #12320 landed in `check-driver-conformance` — closes it, because every intervening specifier is quoted. The four-row table (A/B/C plus **B′**, the no-semicolon case) is in the PR body, and rows B and C are pinned **as a set against each other** rather than against a hand-copied expectation, because order-dependence *was* the defect. That is the right way to pin this.

⭐ **It found a second manifestation the card never described**: the swallow also runs **backwards**, through a preceding `export type EnvironmentDriverRegistry = any;`, leaving a clause beginning with `type` that `isTypeOnlyClause` then discards — so a **real runtime import** vanished through the type-only filter. Independently corroborated by an artifact nobody edited for this: `check-type-source-resolution`'s registry has carried that same pair all along, because it never applies the type-only filter. Two gates disagreeing about one package, explained.

Blast radius measured precisely: `--list` differs by **one line** repo-wide, 303 → 304 pairs, 61-of-72 package count unchanged.

### ⛔ Why it is not landing: the ledger hunk

```diff
-  '@objectstack/hono': ['@objectstack/types'],
+  '@objectstack/hono': ['@objectstack/plugin-hono-server', '@objectstack/types'],
```

`KNOWN_UNALIASED_TEST_IMPORTS`'s own header — read on `origin/main`, not from the PR's quotation of it — says both:

> **MEASURED, not curated** … the **exact set** of unaliased artifact imports

> ⛔ **SHRINK-ONLY. Adding an entry, or widening one, is not how a red build gets fixed** — add the alias to that package's `vitest.config.*` instead.

Those point opposite ways here, and the file does not disambiguate. Adding an entry to a shrink-only ledger is **「抬 ratchet 上限」**, which sits on the maintainer's manual floor **恒交维护者,不论四棱是否同向** — and the floor's stated rationale is precisely this shape: an agent has a structural incentive to widen so CI goes green.

⚠️ To be explicit, because it matters: **the dev's handling of this was exemplary and is not what is being questioned.** It isolated the hunk under "⚠️ One judgment call for review", wrote the mechanism in place beside the change, filed the prescribed remediation as #12767 rather than riding it along, said "reversible in one line", and independently reached the same fork in its own `open_questions` before knowing this escalation existed. **Declaring well is not the same as being entitled to decide** — that gap is exactly what the floor exists to hold, so I am holding it.

Filed as **#12770** with the four-axis analysis and four options (A land as-is · B ride the alias along · C′ land #12767 first, then this · ~~temporary exemption~~ withdrawn). Recommendation **A**, with the standing note that a recommendation is an input, never a clearance.

### State

This card is **`pm:blocked`**, `Blocked-by: #12770`, in the same write. PR #12768 stays **draft**, ⛔ **no auto-merge, not enqueued** — the anti-consensus window stays open. The lane's queue keeps moving; ⛔ the seat does not idle on this.

⚠️ Serial-queue consequence: **#12572 stays undispatchable** — it edits `scripts/check-type-source-resolution.mjs`, which this PR holds until #12770 resolves.

### Out-of-scope finding — verified

**#12767** exists, unassigned, no labels (triage's field), and quotes the gate's prescribed anchored array-form alias with the reason it is separate: it points hono's suite at `plugin-hono-server`'s **source**, so it needs that package's tests actually run. ⭐ It also carries `⛔ Do not resolve this by widening KNOWN_UNALIASED_TEST_IMPORTS` — the dev wrote the guard against its own shipped choice into the follow-up card. That is the honest form of a flagged judgment call.
